answer: Give every agent a cedar-sealed behavioral kernel: a tamper-evident log of its real tasks, tool calls and peer endorsements, verified by independent auditors rather than self-reported. A harbor registry admits an identity only after that kernel shows a sustained, distinct history no other identity shares. Each extra identity then costs a fresh, non-transferable audit plus a bond that doubles — 50, then 100, then 200 POA — so a farm pays exponentially more per fake while a genuine agent pays once.
